'''Joseph Henry Eberly''' (October 19, 1935 – April 30, 2025) was an American physicist and academic. He was a professor of [[physics]], [[astronomy]] and [[optics]] at the [[University of Rochester]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Joseph H. Eberly |url=https://www.lasphys.com/lasphys/personal-card/eberly |access-date=2024-09-13 |website=www.lasphys.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Joseph H. Eberly (1935 – ) |url=https://urresearch.rochester.edu/viewContributorPage.action;jsessionid=E5A1BA96804BD1F4B6AC7C53605186FA?personNameId=4109 |access-date=2024-09-13 |website=urresearch.rochester.edu}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Joseph Henry Eberly was born in 1935. He completed a Bachelor of Science degree in physics at [[Pennsylvania State University]] in 1957 and obtained a Doctor of Philosophy in physics at [[Stanford University]] in 1962. His doctoral advisor during his PhD program was [[Edwin Thompson Jaynes]], which helped him connect with [[Eugene Wigner]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Institute of Optics |url=https://www.sas.rochester.edu/pas/people/faculty/eberly_joseph/index.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230429220608/https://www.sas.rochester.edu/pas/people/faculty/eberly_joseph/index.html |archive-date=2023-04-29 |access-date=2023-12-12 |website=sas.rochester.edu}}</ref> In 1965 he joined he joined the Department of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Rochester, where he worked and continued to teach until a few weeks before his death.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Knispel |first=Sandra |date=May 9, 2025 |title=Pioneering physicist and optical scientist Joseph Eberly remembered |url=https://www.rochester.edu/newscenter/joseph-eberly-physicist-optical-scientist-remembered-651782/ |access-date=May 14, 2025 |website=University of Rochester: News Center}}</ref>

==Work==
Eberly's research interests included [[cavity quantum electrodynamics]] (QED), [[quantum information]], control of non-classical [[Quantum entanglement|entanglement]], the response of [[atom]]s to high-intensity optical pulses, and coherent [[control theory]] of optical interactions.<ref name="University of Rochester">[http://www.optics.rochester.edu/people/faculty/eberly_joseph/index.html Faculty page] at the University of Rochester.</ref> In 1995, he founded the Rochester Theory Center for Optical Science and Engineering (RTC) with funding from the [[National Science Foundation]].<ref name="University of Rochester" />

Eberly contributed to understanding the [[quantum revival]] in the [[Jaynes-Cummings model]].<ref>{{cite journal|author1=J.H. Eberly|author2=N.B. Narozhny|author3=J.J. Sanchez-Mondragon|year=1980|title=Periodic spontaneous collapse and revival in a simple quantum model|journal=Phys. Rev. Lett.|volume=44|issue=20|pages=1323–1326|bibcode=1980PhRvL..44.1323E|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.44.1323}}</ref> In a 1966 paper on electron [[self-energy]], he revealed aspects of the [[Higgs mechanism]] in [[Electromagnetism|electrodynamics]], demonstrating how [[massless particle]]s can acquire mass through interaction with the Higgs field.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Eberly |first1=Joseph H. |last2=Reiss |first2=Howard R. |date=1966-05-27 |title=Electron Self-Energy in Intense Plane-Wave Field |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRev.145.1035 |journal=Physical Review |language=en |volume=145 |issue=4 |pages=1035–1040 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.145.1035 |bibcode=1966PhRv..145.1035E |issn=0031-899X|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Additionally, Eberly studied [[atomic vapor laser isotope separation]].<ref>{{cite book |editor =F. J. Duarte|title=Tunable Laser Applications | edition = 3rd |publisher= [[CRC Press]] |location=Boca Raton |year=2016 |isbn=978-1-4822-6106-6 | author = F. J. Duarte | chapter = Tunable laser atomic vapor laser isotope separation| pages = 371–384 |author-link=F. J. Duarte }}</ref><ref>J. R. Ackerhalt and J. H. Eberly, Coherence versus incoherence in stepwise laser excitation of atoms and molecules, Phys. Rev. A 14, 1705 (1976).</ref>

In 2003, he discovered the phenomenon of [[Space-time crystal|crystallization in time]] for highly excited states of atoms. This phenomenon shows the existence of [[fermion]] densities that are perpetually and perfectly periodic in time, and is comparable to the anomalous conductivity improvement in the [[Kondo effect]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Chan |first1=K. W. |last2=Law |first2=C. K. |last3=Eberly |first3=J. H. |date=2003-08-27 |title=Quantum entanglement in photon-atom scattering |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevA.68.022110 |journal=Physical Review A |language=en |volume=68 |issue=2 |article-number=022110 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.68.022110 |bibcode=2003PhRvA..68b2110C |issn=1050-2947|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

He made early predictions of the phenomenon of the [[Above-threshold ionization|Above Threshold Ionization]] (ATI) and the highly energetic electron emissions in one-dimensional atom models. He also observed a similar phenomenon in the emission of highly energetic [[deuterium]] nuclei from the ultra-cold strong [[Coulomb explosion|laser driven deuterium droplet clusters]]. {{Edition needed|date=September 2024}} These clusters are considered alike to giant atom with [[deuteron]]s acting as heavy electrons, and the electrons acting as their [[gluon]]s or nucleus. Eberly also observed the [[Cold fusion|cold]]-hot [[Nuclear Fusion|nuclear fusion]] in such systems.<ref>T. Ditmire, J. Zweiback, V. P. Yanovsky. T. E. Cowan. G. Hays and K. B. Wharton, Nuclear fusion from explosions of femtosecond laser-heated deuterium clusters, Nature 398, 6727 (1999)</ref>

==Death and legacy==
Eberly died April 30, 2025, at the age of 89.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.optica.org/about/newsroom/obituaries/2025/obituary |title=In Memoriam: Joseph Eberly, 1935–2025 |website=optica.org |date=April 30, 2025 |access-date=May 3, 2025}}</ref> In January 2026, the University of Rochester announced the establishment of the Joseph H. Eberly Endowed Professorship in Physics and the Joseph H. Eberly Endowed Professorship Research Fund.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Campaign |first1=For Ever Better |last2=Ferguson |first2=Barbara |date=2026-01-26 |title=Honoring a legend: Joseph Eberly's family endows physics professorship and research fund in his memory |url=https://everbetter.rochester.edu/honoring-a-legend-the-eberly-family-endows-physics-professorship-and-research-fund-in-memory-of-joseph-eberly/ |access-date=2026-01-27 |website=For Ever Better Campaign |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
Eberly received the [[Charles Hard Townes]] Award,<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1994-06-01 |title=OSA Prize Winners Reflect a Wide Range of Achievements |journal=Physics Today |volume=47 |issue=6 |pages=89–90 |doi=10.1063/1.2808540 |bibcode=1994PhT....47f..89. |issn=0031-9228}}</ref> the [[Marian Smoluchowski Medal|Smoluchowski Medal]] and the Senior Humboldt Award.<ref>[http://old.ptf.net.pl/ptf3.html Recipients of the Smoluchowski Medal].</ref> In 2007, he served as the president of [[Optica (society)|The Optical Society of America]].<ref name="Optica">[http://www.osa.org/en-us/history/biographies/joseph-eberly/ Biography] from The Optical Society of America.</ref> In recognition of his work on the theory of electron localization in atoms and molecules, he was honored with the [[Frederic Ives Medal]] in 2010,<ref>http://www.osa.org/Awards_and_Grants/Awards/Award_Description/ivesquinn/default.aspx Recipients of Frederic Ives Medal / Quinn Prize</ref> the highest award granted by The Optical Society of America. In 2012, the society recognized his many years of service with the Distinguished Service Award.<ref name="Optica" /> In 2021, he was appointed an honorary member of [[Optica (society)|Optica]] (formerly The Optical Society of America).<ref>[https://www.rochester.edu/newscenter/joseph-Eberly-2021-honorary-member-of-Optica-503732/ Joseph Eberly] honored as a 'true visionary' in Optics.</ref>

Eberly had longstanding research connections with [[Poland]], publishing several papers with Polish physicists Adam Kujawski and Krzysztof Wódkiewicz in the 1960s and 1970s.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Kujawski |first1=A. |last2=Eberly |first2=J. H. |chapter=On Solutions Describing Self-Induced Transparency of Ultra-Short Pulses |date=1978 |editor-last=Mandel |editor-first=Leonard |editor2-last=Wolf |editor2-first=Emil |title=Coherence and Quantum Optics IV |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-1-4757-0665-9_98 |language=en |location=Boston, MA |publisher=Springer US |pages=989–997 |doi=10.1007/978-1-4757-0665-9_98 |isbn=978-1-4757-0665-9}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Eberly |first1=J. H. |last2=Kujawski |first2=A. |date=1967-04-10 |title=Statistical homogeneity, isotropy, and time-stationarity |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0375960167902204 |journal=Physics Letters A |volume=24 |issue=8 |pages=426–428 |doi=10.1016/0375-9601(67)90220-4 |bibcode=1967PhLA...24..426E |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wBB9L4bUw60 Leading Eberly's collaborator from Poland [[Iwo Białynicki-Birula]] granted Wigner Medal for co-discoveries</ref> He maintained a frequent scientific collaboration with [[Iwo Białynicki-Birula]] and was elected as a foreign member of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Division III: Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Earth Sciences |work=Polish Academy of Sciences |url=https://pan.pl/en/division-iii/}}</ref> Eberly also co-authored multiple publications with Białynicki-Birula's PhD student [[Kazimierz Rzążewski]]. Their collaboration led to the discovery that the [[superradiant phase transition]], originally observed at the University of Rochester, necessitates the existence of an "extraterrestrial" ether with a real and negative [[dielectric constant]] in the quantum vacuum.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Rzążewski |first1=K. |last2=Wódkiewicz |first2=K. |last3=Żakowicz |first3=W. |date=1975-08-18 |title=Two-Level Atoms, and the 𝐴2 Term|url=https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.35.432 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=35|page=432 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.35.432 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> This finding challenged the notion that classical electromagnetic gauge fields alone could cause such a [[phase transition]], aligning with the electromagnetic version of the [[Bohr–van Leeuwen theorem|Bohr-van Leeuwen theorem]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Białynicki-Birula |first1=I. |last2=Rzążewski |first2=K.| date=1979-01-01 |title=No-go theorem concerning the superradiant phase transition in atomic systems|url=https://journals.aps.org/pra/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevA.19.301 |journal=Physical Review A |volume=19|issue=1 |page=301 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.19.301 |bibcode=1979PhRvA..19..301B |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Publications==
Eberly published over 350 scientific journal articles, as well as other scientific papers. He also authored three graduate textbooks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Joseph H. Eberly − Publications |url=https://academictree.org/physics/publications.php?pid=71783 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220427033925/https://academictree.org/physics/publications.php?pid=71783 |archive-date=2022-04-27 |access-date=2022-04-27 |website=academictree.org}}</ref>
